newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER AS RATES REMAIN STEADY.
newsitem.headline: CANADA DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER AS RATES REMAIN STEADY.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar closed weaker at C$1.3930 (US$0.7179) in quiet trading on Monday. * Analysts said this morning's weak housing data and the failure of the Bank of Canada to hike interest rates weighed on the currency. * Further weakness was expected as currency traders test the central bank's resolve to defend the unit.
The Canadian dollar closed weaker in quiet trading on Monday as weak housing data and the failure of the Bank of Canada to hike interest rates weighed on the currency.
The currency softened to C$1.3930 (US$0.7179), extending losses after opening weaker at C$1.3923 (US$0.7182).

"It's a little bit of disappointment over the Canadian housing starts numbers," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with I.D.E.A. "It's just really the fact that there are no rate hikes right now and that's just keeping the forex traders testing the Bank of Canada's resolve."

Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp this morning reported that Canadian housing starts rose by 2.7 percent in July to a seasonally adjusted rate of 144,700 units from a revised 140,900 in June. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a gain of 147,125 units for July.

Analysts said the weaker than expected report made it less likely that the Bank of Canada would hike interest rates. Many foreign exchange traders hope for a rate hike because it would likely strengthen the currency by luring capital flows into Canada.
Financial markets were expected to continue putting pressure on the currency to test the central bank's resolve.

"I think we'll see it test the C$1.3970 (US$0.7158) range," said one corporate dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. The dealers said trading was light during today's session and that the currency managed a comeback as the unit headed toward C$1.3950 (US$0.7168).
On the crosses, the Canada dollar climbed to 83.35 Japanese yen from 82.34 on Friday and rose to 1.3376 marks from Friday's 1.3269 marks.
